identity.title: Antigen scaffolds drive preferential expansion of functional genetically engineered CAR and TCR T cells.

content.abstract: T cells engineered to express recombinant T cell receptors (TCRs) or chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) can induce durable clinical responses in solid and hematological malignancies. However, manufacturing is resource intensive and often yields highly differentiated, exhausted T cell products. To address this, we developed an antigen-scaffold (Ag-scaffold) technology that presents cognate antigen alongside stimulatory cytokines to preferentially expand genetically engineered T cells. We expanded CRISPR-Cas9- and lentivirally engineered TCR T cells with peptide MHC (pMHC)-presenting Ag-scaffolds and anti-CD19 CAR T cells with CD19-presenting Ag-scaffolds. By applying cognate pMHC Ag-scaffolds, we achieved on average 69% (+/-22%) antigen-specific T cells after 14 days of culture with a cytotoxic, proliferative profile. Ag-scaffold expansion enhanced initial TCR and CAR cytotoxicity; repeated rechallenges showed sustained control. In vivo, Ag-scaffold-expanded CRISPR-Cas9-engineered NY-ESO-1-specific TCR T cells and anti-CD19 CAR T cells also showed improved tumor control in lymphoma and solid tumor xenograft models compared to cells expanded with IL2/7/15.
